newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez Lyonnaise holds 1997 profit forecast. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Suez Lyonnaise holds 1997 profit forecast. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects name of company in headline and text from Lyonnaise/Suez.)
A spokeswoman for the newly-merged Lyonnaise des Eaux and Cie de Suez utilities group said on Thursday it was maintaining its forecast for a net attributable profit of 3.5 billion francs for 1997.
The forecast took into account the impact of the windfall tax on utilities levied by the British government in Wednesday's budget.
Payments by the group's British subsidiary Northumbrian Water Group Plc had been taken into account in the profit forecast, she said.
"It does not affect our forecast for results for 1997 which remain above 3.5 billion francs for the Groupe Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux," she said.
"Based on initial calculations the charge will be 79 million stg, payable in two times," for Northumbrian, she said.
Given Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux's 70 percent holding in Northumbrian, the payment came "as no surprise", she added.
The 1996 proforma net attributable profit for the group was two billion francs, she said.

Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on Wednesday announced details of a special windfall tax on privatised utility companies to raise around 5.2 billion stg, aimed at funding job creation measures and capital investment in schools.
